items.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Moody’s word of mouth has gotten me a lot of gigs. And he’s been very supportive, very helpful, and as I was mentioning, he often calls me up and plays a lick over the phone for me... Holly has played alongside Frank Wess, Slide Hampton, and James Moody

ctx.x: I didn’t. But yes, I’ve heard him live many times, and I’m just in awe of what he can do, especially considering that he still doubles to this day. And many of the flute players, including Hubert Laws, well Moody still doubles, I’m thinking Herbie Mann, a lot of those guys just don’t double anymore because it’s a tremendous embouchure change. And it’s been really — the fact that he does it so well, it just amazes me. When I on the other hand tried to play saxophone in college, because everybody told me that I…
Ooh. Ouch. Did he say this in front of the—

items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Like you have your Holly Hofmann, wonderful flautist here, wonderful, and Charles McPherson, he lives here, Daniel Jackson, he’s here. Who’s the piano player, honey, and the bass player that used to work at Lario’s? Bob Magnusson, and Holly’s piano player.

ctx.x: You’ve got to charge up your batteries to keep up with it.

Yeah, man. And you know there are good musicians here you know, but they don’t support it man. Like you have your Holly Hofmann, wonderful flautist here, wonderful, and Charles McPherson, he lives here, Daniel Jackson, he’s here. Who’s the piano player, honey, and the bass player that used to work at Lario’s? Bob Magnusson, and Holly’s piano player.
